Where agents run · required
  A computer of yours, or sandboxes at boat.dev on your own account.
<QR>
  1. A computer
     The hub's own machine can run agents too. In the app, Settings › Hub › Machines › Add machine does each of these.
     The hub's own machine, on it:
       fleetd machine add --local
     Another machine, on the hub:
       fleetd pair --worker <name>
       The hub is only at http://HUB, which no other machine reaches, so only a node on the hub's own computer can join it. For another machine, give the hub its tailnet or LAN address: on the hub, run fleetd init --listen <ip>:<port> --url http://<name>:<port> (Settings › Hub › Setup › Where the hub listens), then try again.
<QR>
  2. Or hosted sandboxes
     Make an API key at the provider and paste it in Settings › Hub › Machines › Providers; the app seals it on your device. Each agent runs in a sandbox of its own there, with its browser, Linux desktop and Android, billed to your account while it runs.
     boat.dev › API keys: https://docs.boat.dev/api-keys
     Key name:
       fleetd on hub
<QR>
  3. Android screens (optional)
     Android emulators run on any Linux machine with KVM: the first one installs itself. iOS simulators are the agents' Mac's: A Mac for agents sets it up.
<QR>
  In the app: Settings › Hub › Machines.
<QR>
  Test: Read each computer's checks, and list fleetd's sandboxes at each connected provider.
✗  Where agents run required: A computer of yours, or sandboxes at boat.dev on your own account. Fix: fleetd init --step machines

Run fleetd init --step machines again when you've done it; it keeps what's done.
